previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, chronic pancreatitis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for persistent left lower extremity cellulitis that failed outpatient treatment with minocycline. She presented with severe pain, swelling, spreading erythema, and fever. IV vancomycin was initiated empirically due to prior MRSA history and lack of response. Imaging ruled out osteomyelitis and DVT. Wound culture identified methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, prompting a switch to oral clindamycin. She developed non-allergic hives during admission, managed supportively. Her infection improved clinically, with reduced erythema and normalizing labs. She was discharged home on clindamycin, with instructions to continue chronic medications, use ACE wraps, and follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Cellulitis and LLE pain: Pt was treated with IV vancomycin 
throughout hospitalization, and infection was improving. She was 
discharged with a PICC and to complete the course of IV 
vancomycin. Dermatology was consulted, who suggested that the 
patient discontinues use of silver chloride as may be irritating 
ulcer. 
Per dermatology recommendations, for her chronic left malleolal 
ulcer dermatology recommended diluted vinegar soaks (1 part 
vinegar to 10 parts water). Gauze dressings
may be wetted with the dilute acetic acid solution and applied 
to
the ulcer for 15 minutes per day before dressing the wound. 
Dermatology also recommended continue treating with topical 
mupirocin ointment
followed by adaptic, telfa and kerlix dressings.
.
# Positive UA, but asymptomatic on ROS. Patient may have 
asymptomatic bacturia, which does not warrant antibiotics 
treatment in an elderly woman. Follow-up urine culture revealed 
contaminant. Pt was not treated for UTI.
.
CHRONIC ISSUES:
# HTN: Pt was normotensive during hospitalization and maintained 
on metoprolol as outpatient.
.
# Chronic pancreatitis: Stable during hospitalization, pt was 
given outpatient regimen of pancreatic enzyme replacement.
.
# GERD: Stable, pt was continued on outpatient medications. 
.
# Restless leg syndrome: Stable, and pt was continued on home 
pramipexole
